prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a quiet change is appearing in the way many young Japanese people think about travel.

The dream is becoming slower and more personal. Travelers want more control over their time. They want to travel at their own pace, follow their interests, and leave some parts of the trip open.

Several independent surveys point in the same direction. One survey found strong interest among young men in solo travel or trips built around personal hobbies. Another found that about 90% of Japanese Gen Z travelers with overseas travel experience wanted free time during a tour. About 80% wanted at least half a day.

But there is a twist.

When people were asked what they would do if they could take a full month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. That answer was chosen by about 24% of respondents.

In real travel plans, however, the stays were much shorter. An autumn survey found an average of 1.8 nights, with a median of 2 nights.

So the story is not that young Japanese travelers have already moved completely from sightseeing to long, slow stays. The stronger change is in what they want from a trip. Their wishes are becoming more flexible and personal, while their actual time away remains limited.

A national tourism report makes the same tension visible. It says Japan still needs to increase the number of trips per person and make stays longer. In other words, the wish for a slower trip is clear, but it has not fully become longer behavior yet.

【Point One】
The change also differs by gender. Among men under 30, about a quarter chose solo travel, and a similar share chose hobby-focused travel in one survey. Among women under 30, food travel led at just over half, while visiting famous tourist sites reached about 45%. Travel businesses may need to separate trips built around independence and personal interests from trips centered on famous landmarks.

【Point Two】
The gap is not only about the number of nights. A short trip may still be designed around choice, with optional activities and open time. The survey results suggest that half a day without fixed plans can matter, even when a much longer holiday is difficult. At the same time, policy must still work on the larger challenge of lengthening stays.

point_one.reasoning: 男女別の具体的な旅行嗜好を示し、男性向けの自立・趣味重視型と女性に多い食や有名観光地重視型を分けて考える必要性を示している。Full Storyにはない性別差と、旅行事業者への具体的な示唆が加わっている。

point_two.reasoning: 短い旅行でも自由時間や選択肢を組み込めるという示唆はあるが、Full Storyが既に述べた「個人の裁量を求める一方、実際の滞在は短い」という中心的な緊張関係の言い換えに近い。政策面の長期滞在化にも新しい具体性はほとんど加わっていない。
